2608.14522.title: Participatory Moral AI Is Not Neutral: The Invisible Hand of Developers
2608.14522.paper_summary: As AI systems make more morally loaded decisions across society, one response has been moral preference elicitation. In this approach, researchers poll participants on hypothetical dilemmas and use the aggregated votes to train a policy that an AI model then applies at scale. Before any vote is cast, developers make three key choices in the moral AI elicitation pipeline: feature scoping, voter sampling, and question framing. In other words, they decide which features go to a vote, which voters to include, and how to present the question. These choices are often opaque, undocumented, and treated as technical details rather than normative ones. We examine each of these choices within a common empirical study and show that each can shape the preferences produced by moral AI elicitation. Across two phases (N = 809) in three deployment contexts (i.e., AI kidney allocation, AI agents simulating absent workers, and generative AI depictions of the deceased), we examine the three main stages of the moral AI elicitation pipeline. First, morally relevant features shift across contexts. This suggests that feature schemas should not be assumed to transfer across deployment domains. Second, preferences differ by political ideology for roughly one-third of features, with some differences reversing direction. The ideological composition of the voter pool can therefore affect the resulting aggregated preference profile. Third, the wording of the elicitation question can narrow or widen ideological gaps by up to a full scale point. The framing conditions also change how moral foundations are associated with participants' judgments. Taken together, these findings suggest that voting-based alignment cannot deliver fair or transparent AI by aggregation alone; at minimum, each stage of the moral AI elicitation pipeline should be audited and disclosed.
2608.14522.paper_summary_zh: 隨著人工智慧系統在社會中做出越來越多道德上負載的決策，一種回應是道德偏好引導。在這種方法中，研究人員對參與者進行假設性困境的調查，並使用聚合的投票結果來訓練一個政策，然後由人工智慧模型在大規模上應用。在任何投票之前，開發者在道德人工智慧引導流程中做出三個關鍵選擇：特徵範圍、選民抽樣和問題框架。換句話說，他們決定哪些特徵進行投票、包括哪些選民，以及如何呈現問題。這些選擇通常是不透明的、沒有文檔記錄的，並被視為技術細節而非規範性問題。我們在一個共同的實證研究中檢視這些選擇，並顯示每個選擇都可以塑造道德人工智慧引導所產生的偏好。在三個部署情境中的兩個階段（N = 809）（即人工智慧腎臟分配、模擬缺席工作者的人工智慧代理和生成性人工智慧對已故者的描繪），我們檢視了道德人工智慧引導流程的三個主要階段。首先，道德相關特徵在不同情境中有所變化。這表明特徵範疇不應假設可以跨部署領域轉移。其次，約三分之一的特徵在政治意識形態上存在差異，某些差異甚至會反向。選民池的意識形態組成因此可以影響最終的聚合偏好輪廓。第三，引導問題的措辭可以將意識形態差距縮小或擴大多達整個量表的一點。框架條件也改變了道德基礎與參與者判斷的關聯。綜合來看，這些發現表明，僅依賴投票基於聚合無法提供公平或透明的人工智慧；至少，道德人工智慧引導流程的每個階段都應進行審計和披露。
